Make the paused-empty scenario use chronologically older backlog data, assert that the first post-event resume is a fresh head request rather than an old-cursor request, and add a failing old-cursor mutation control. Add a held-opening real reconnect scenario with no later message trigger. Rerun the affected tests, the full project-owned npm run test:tela suite, and the repeated FRC evidence against the resulting source manifest; retain existing unchanged API evidence. findings.title: [P2] Opening-race coverage omits reconnect while the initial response is held
findings.rationale: web-app/e2e/timeline.spec.ts:56 proves a real inbound message during a held opening response, but not an onopen/reconnect callback in that same threadAtual-null state. src/tempoReal.spec.ts:25 uses a fake socket to prove callback emission, while the browser reconnect case at web-app/e2e/timeline.spec.ts:121 begins after opening has completed. A regression that suppresses or misroutes the reconnect callback only while invalidacaoAbertura is active would pass all supplied assertions, despite the approved requirement that reconnection recover without a further event or poll.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): hold the actual opening GET after its backend fetch, force a real socket reconnect while it remains pending, and require a read-neutral recovery without a later message event or clock advance; assert current IDs and unread after release. B: add an equivalent browser-level controllable real-socket integration case. C: rely on the helper unit test plus the post-opening reconnect test, which does not protect this opening-generation transition.

findings.title: [P2] Empty-thread recovery test does not prove restart from the new head
findings.rationale: web-app/e2e/timeline.spec.ts:181 seeds the 160-message burst at Date.now()+10_000, then sends both inbound webhooks through a fixture that supplies no message timestamp (api-app/test/timeline-fixtures.cjs:57). The final run completes far inside that ten-second offset, so receipt-time inbound messages are older than the entire burst. A broken paused-empty branch that retains its old cursor can load the remaining ten burst rows plus the two older inbound rows after Continue, still reach 162 IDs and unread=2, and never issue the required fresh-head read. The test counts only the initial three requests and never asserts that the first request after the between-round event has no antes cursor. It therefore does not discriminate the ARCH-DEL-02 regression or prove current metadata refresh in that path.
findings.suggested_action: A (recommended): seed the burst in the past so each real inbound event is newer, instrument the resumed request and require a read-neutral recent-page request without antes before any older traversal, then retain complete ID/unread and visible current-metadata assertions. Add a mutation that retains the old empty-thread cursor and require this regression to fail. B: provide explicit inbound timestamps later than the burst with the same request-level assertion. C: retain final-state equality alone, which leaves the reviewed stale-cursor behavior unprotected.
